tasks.gr11-social-environmental-responsibility: Topic: Social and Environmental Responsibility. Cover environmental justice, sustainability principles, social justice frameworks, accountability at individual and institutional level, and responsible community action. Ask Grade 11 learners to evaluate a local environmental or social challenge, argue for an ethical response, explain the relationship between sustainability and human rights, or propose actions an individual or school could take.
tasks.gr11-community-participation-t2: Topic: Community Participation. Cover the purpose and forms of volunteering and community service, qualities of effective community leadership, planning a campaign or project to address a real community need, identifying support services, and collaboration strategies. Ask Grade 11 learners to design a community project proposal, evaluate a participation scenario, describe leadership qualities needed, or reflect on the impact of civic involvement.
tasks.gr11-risk-and-wellbeing-t2: Topic: Risk and Wellbeing. Cover the causes and effects of substance abuse, the impact of trauma and violence on individuals and communities, healthy coping strategies and stress management, protective factors that reduce risk, and available support networks and services. Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse a risk scenario, identify protective vs risk factors, explain the consequences of substance abuse, or describe support services and when to access them.
tasks.gr11-physical-education-task-2-t2: Topic: Physical Education Task — Term 2. Cover team sport skills, tactical and strategic play, leadership and communication within a team, the value of fair play, and how participation in group activity supports overall wellness. Ask Grade 11 learners to evaluate team roles, reflect on leadership in physical activity, describe a strategy used in a team sport, or keep a wellness record tracking activity and mood.
tasks.gr11-study-styles-annual-plan-t2: Topic: Study styles, strategies and the annual study plan (Grade 11 Life Orientation, Term 2). Cover study skills, styles and strategies, exam writing skills including time per mark, and building an annual plan with measurable goals. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
